audit.why: full phases[N].side and content win[N] agree row for row and match the packet: Akshan 1-3, Skill at 4-5 and 6, Master Yi at first item and 2+ items. The mirror kept the same read.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike is described without a single cooldown, and it calls Comeuppance an execute.
audit.why: Comeuppance stores bullets and deals damage based on missing health — no threshold. Its cooldown is 100/85/70s, Heroic Swing is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s, Highlander is a flat 85s.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text and phases[4].why now carry the real timers and the real R behaviour.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[5].t states outright that Alpha Strike's untargetability 'dodges nothing of his'. It answers his single biggest damage source: Comeuppance fires stored bullets at a locked target, and untargetability blanks it. Separately, two places say Akshan 'revives off his passive' — the revive is on Going Rogue (W) and it resurrects his dead allies when he kills a Scoundrel, not himself. Camouflage is the W active, not a passive.
audit.why: One tells the player to throw away their best defensive tool; the other invents a self-revive that will make a player abandon a won fight.
audit.corrected: Alpha Strike blanks a fired Comeuppance. Going Rogue (W, 18/14/10/6/2s) grants camouflage and carries the Scoundrel revive of his ALLIES. Dirty Fighting (P) is a shield-and-bonus-damage proc every third hit plus an extra reduced-damage attack.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[11].t lists 'eating his revive' as a common mistake.
audit.why: That mistake does not exist. The real second mistake is spending Alpha Strike on the chase instead of holding it for Comeuppance.

edits.before: Roughly even. His R (Comeuppance) is a long-range execute but he needs W camouflage and E swing to reposition; your Highlander and Q Alpha Strike let you close, though he can W away if unpunished.
edits.after: Roughly even. Comeuppance (R, 100s at rank 1) scales with your missing health — it is not an execute, and Alpha Strike's untargetability blanks the fired bullets. Highlander's flat 85s slow immunity is how you close.

edits.before: Alpha Strike's untargetable blink dodges nothing of his (his kit is skillshot/auto), but Highlander's slow immunity is what lets you ignore his slows and close the gap his E swing tries to recreate; Meditate's damage reduction and heal is what neutralizes his Avengerang poke war.
edits.after: Alpha Strike's untargetable blink hard-answers Comeuppance (R) — go untargetable as the stored bullets fire and the whole cast is wasted. Highlander's slow immunity is what lets you ignore his slows and close the gap his E swing recreates; Meditate's damage reduction neutralizes his Avengerang poke war.

edits.before: If you fall behind, his lethality build one-shots your squishy frame from range and your Alpha Strike won't close the gap before he E-swings away or revives off passive — farm side waves, take Wit's End/armor, and look to teamfight where his single-target poke matters less.
edits.after: If you fall behind, his lethality build chunks you from range and Alpha Strike won't close before he E-swings away. Once you have killed one of his allies you are marked a Scoundrel and your death revives them — farm side waves, take Wit's End/armor, and fight where his poke matters less.

edits.before: Outside of Highlander you'll never catch him — his E swing plus camouflage passive resets the gap, and you'll walk into a turret dive or his revive.
edits.after: Outside of Highlander you'll never catch him — his E swing (18s at rank 1) plus Going Rogue camouflage resets the gap, and you walk into a turret dive.

edits.before: Highlander gives slow immunity to threaten an all-in, but Akshan's camouflage passive and E swing let him reset distance, so it's a coin-flip on whether you stick.
edits.after: Highlander gives slow immunity to threaten an all-in, but his W camouflage (18s at rank 1) and E swing let him reset distance, so it's a coin-flip on whether you stick.

edits.before: The classic Yi mistake here is Alpha-Striking onto a full-HP Akshan to 'trade' early — it burns your only escape into a ranged kiter and you lose the HP race; the second is chasing him without Highlander slow immunity and eating a dive or his revive.
edits.after: The classic Yi mistake here is Alpha-Striking onto a full-HP Akshan to 'trade' early — it burns your only escape into a ranged kiter and you lose the HP race; the second is spending Alpha Strike on the chase instead of saving it to blank his Comeuppance.

notes: Akshan has no self-revive anywhere in his kit; Going Rogue resurrects his dead ALLIES when he kills the Scoundrel who killed them. Any Master Yi or other page saying 'he revives off passive' is wrong. Not verified and therefore left off the page: whether Alpha Strike's untargetability cancels a Comeuppance that has already begun releasing bullets versus only preventing the lock-on, and whether Heroic Swing's collision knock-off triggers on an untargetable Yi.
